title: Learning from data
subtitle: Instead of writing rules, show examples and let an optimiser find the rule.

kinds.title: Kinds of learning
kinds.body: Supervised learning has labelled examples (input → correct output): classification (discrete labels) and regression (numbers). Unsupervised learning finds structure without labels: clustering, dimensionality reduction. Reinforcement learning learns from rewards by trial and error. Semi-supervised uses a few labels plus many unlabelled examples. The four pillars of the field: data, model, loss and optimiser.

gd.title: Gradient descent
gd.body: To minimise a loss f(x), repeatedly step opposite the slope: x ← x − η f′(x), with learning rate η. Too small is slow; too large overshoots and can diverge. On f(x) = x² − 4x + 5 with η = 0.2 it converges to x = 2; with f(x) = x² and η = 1.1 each step multiplies x by −1.2 and it diverges (yes).
gd.steps: f(x) = x² − 4x + 5, f′(x) = 2x − 4. Start x = −1, η = 0.2. Step 1: slope −6, so x ← −1 − 0.2(−6) = 0.2. Continuing converges to the minimum where f′ = 0, x = 2.

reg.title: Linear regression
reg.body: Fit ŷ = b₀ + b₁x by minimising the sum of squared residuals. The closed form: b₁ = Sxy/Sxx and b₀ = ȳ − b₁x̄. For the five sample points: slope 0.9, intercept 1.3, R² = 0.81 (the fraction of variance explained). The same idea extends to many features and, with a sigmoid, to logistic regression for classification.

cluster.title: Clustering: k-means
cluster.body: k-means alternates: assign every point to its nearest centroid; move each centroid to the mean of its points; repeat until nothing changes. It minimises the within-cluster sum of squares but depends on the start and on k. On the sample points the centroids settle at (1.25,1.5) (3.9,5.1).

perc.title: The perceptron and overfitting
perc.body: A perceptron classifies by the sign of w·x + b and corrects itself on mistakes: w ← w + η(t − y)x. It converges on linearly separable data (AND: converged yes in 6 epochs) and never on data like XOR. Models can overfit — memorise noise in the training data — so performance is measured on held-out data, hyper-parameters are tuned on a validation set, and cross-validation rotates the split. Underfitting means the model is too simple to capture the pattern.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Learning = data + model + loss + optimiser.
  • Gradient descent: x ← x − η f′(x); watch η.
  • Evaluate on unseen data; precision/recall beyond accuracy.
